Same instrument, opposite framework. **Why it matters:** If Forward Guidance is right, long-end yields are being artificially suppressed and inflation expectations should be repriced higher — sell duration, buy real assets. If Howell is right, this is structural plumbing and yields will compress toward nominal GDP naturally. V16 regime detection should be sensitive to which interpretation the bond market is pricing. *Severity: 7/10.*

**[BLIND_SPOT] — Energy Shock Not Reflected in Broad Data**

The IC sources are screaming energy stress; the data monitoring layer is silent. This gap is either because stress hasn't propagated to monitored instruments yet, or the 25-asset universe lacks direct diesel/refinery exposure. **Why it matters:** If this is a genuine supply shock, it will transmit to: credit (transport/industrial), equities (energy sector divergence), and inflation (re-acceleration). F6 should be scanning energy-adjacent unusual options flow aggressively. *Severity: 8/10.*

Consensus on "performative hawkishness" is now crowded. **Why it matters:** If September FOMC delivers any balance sheet surprise or unexpected tone shift, positioning in rate-sensitive assets gets dislocated. The trap is complacency around Fed inaction. *Severity: 5/10.*
